title: Discussion and Conclusion
paragraphs: Chapter 7 Discussion and Conclusion Chapter abstract. This chapter interprets the results for EST, mass-communication scholarship, platform design, and future research. It separates what the evidence supports from what remains speculative, discusses the epistemicengagement tradeo, the narrow lter activity, the failure of the semantic block to improve prediction, and the limits of the sample. It closes with the thesis conclusion and a eld-study agenda. 7.1 What the Results Mean for EST This thesis develops EST as an original account of the relationship between platform architecture, audience evaluation, and epistemic governance. Its contribution combines theory construction, the LOKLOK platform design, a eld questionnaire, and a separate model-based comparison. These components answer dierent questions. The survey describes audience judgments in a particular listening setting; the simulation explores the consequences of specied architectural rules. Neither component should be interpreted as a universal verication of the whole theory. Table 7.1 states the proposition-level verdicts without collapsing measured, model-based, and prospective evidence into one status. 220

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 221 Table 7.1: EST Propositions, Hypotheses, Evidence, and Verdicts Proposition Hypothesis Evidence in this thesis Verdict EST-P1: architecture shapes structural credibility H1, H4, H5 Measured PBstar and BRS associations; model BRS path; no eld randomisation Partial; model-conditional, not a eld causal claim EST-P2: diversity and cooling constrain epistemic concentration H2 MORE/Lagrange is the dominant model path; cooling and echo terms are implemented; topology check is networkindependent Supported within the model; eld mechanism untested EST-P3: measurement must be accountable H3 BRS/PB internal consistency is high; single-factor CFA t is poor; multigroup invariance not estimated Mixed: reliability supported, structural validity not established EST-P4: participatory performance is the educational test H7 Prospective claim-appraisal task; no human task data Untested; future study required Note. H1H7 are dened in Chapter 1. Supported within the model means the specied outcome equations and ablations imply the pattern; it does not mean a human eld eect has been estimated. The semantic block is contextual, not the driver of the contrast. In short, H1 is partially supported but not identied as a eld eect; H2 is supported within the model; H3 is mixed because reliability is high but structural validity is not established; H4 is associational; H5 and H6 are exploratory model checks; and H7 is prospective. The conclusion therefore keeps the model-based trade-o as the central nding and the human causal claim as future work.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 222 7.1.1 RQ1: Structural Determination The eld results show that PB scores are positively related to the overall star rating, broadcaster-rating dimensions, duration, and reported interaction. The model additionally predicts higher PB and star ratings under the epistemic-rst conguration. Together, these ndings make architectural inuence a useful research proposition. However, the eld sample contains no random assignment of architecture and no identied comparison of the relative contributions of architecture and user characteristics. The strong version of structural dominance in EST-P1 remains a hypothesis for direct testing, not an estimated result of the correlation analysis. 7.1.2 RQ2: Diversity and the Thermodynamic Analogy The model reports changes in ECO and correction acceptance and an engagement trade-o under its specied rules. Those outputs give EST-P2 a concrete modelbased formulation. The eld interactionPB gradient, however, is not a measurement of information entropy, network mixing, or correction dynamics. It cannot independently demonstrate the thermodynamic analogy. The formal language is useful insofar as it species an objective and observable predictions; it does not replace evidence that the real platform follows the specied dynamics. 7.1.3 RQ3: Psychometric Accountability The supplied R outputs give high internal-consistency coecients, but the factor-t results do not establish the proposed measurement structure. This is a substantive nding rather than a detail to conceal behind the sample size. It limits claims about

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 223 what the BRS and PB aggregates measure. The result is compatible with EST-P3 as a requirement for measurement accountability, while failing to establish H3's stronger claim that the instruments already satisfy the full validity requirement. PB combines judgments about condence, diversity, comparative trustion, structural clarity, and quality. These may covary without being interchangeable. The very high associations of PB with SV and IQ likewise require examination of discriminant validity. An audience can regard a broadcast as credible without its claims being accurate, and an intention to verify is not the same as observed verication. Consequently, the present scores should describe respondents' evaluations rather than certify broadcaster competence or student achievement. 7.1.4 RQ4: Integration of the Constructs The positive pattern of correlations supports studying the constructs together. It does not distinguish a shared epistemic-quality trait from common-method variation or overlapping item content. The original Bayesian summary places most predictive weight on IQ while reporting collinearity. That coecient is therefore an association within the specied model, not evidence that IQ is the unique cause of the other evaluations. A future measurement study should compare plausible alternative structures and include criteria that do not come from the same response occasion. 7.2 Relation to Mass Communication Scholarship The thesis places audience evaluation within a platform rather than treating it as an isolated opinion. Its six-dimensional review connects institutional ltering, at-

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 224 tention, misinformation diusion, parasocial relationships, measurement, and educational opportunity. EST integrates these concerns into one proposed design-oriented framework; the individual literatures remain sources of evidence and competing explanations rather than proofs of the new theory. The observed starPB correlation suggests convergence between a familiar summary rating and a multi-item evaluation. This is relevant to mass communication research because audience metrics frequently compress dierent judgments into one visible number. The result does not show that the star rating or PB is a substitute for content analysis. Source credibility, message credibility, and overall experience must remain distinguishable when interpreting a platform's reputation display. The ride setting also matters. The durationPB and interactionPB associations may reect opportunity for exposure, content preferences, conversational involvement, prior interest, or selection into longer journeys. The study does not identify which explanation dominates. Its contribution is to document those contextual relationships and make them explicit in the framework, rather than generalise from the journey setting to all university listening or to all forms of social audio. The radio-specic case is a scope condition, not a claim about social media in general. The mechanism may transfer, but the instruments, stimuli, and outcome semantics would require revalidation in text, image, or video settings.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 225 7.3 Implications for Platform Design LOKLOK provides a concrete specication of reputation display, recommendation constraints, reective prompts, and integrity review. The simulation permits comparison of alternative objective functions before deployment. In the reported model, epistemic-rst settings increase some perceived-quality indicators while reducing raw engagement. The trade-o index of −.290 is a model-specic summary, not an inevitable cost that every platform must pay. Field evaluation must establish whether the predicted directions and magnitudes survive changes in participants, content, and implementation. The BRS display should distinguish an audience-derived evaluation from a fact-checking judgment. Any uncertainty interval shown to users needs a validated measurement procedure; attaching an interval to an unreliable or misinterpreted score does not solve the underlying problem. The same caution applies to moderation and coordination ags: a detector's output should not be presented as certain misconduct without a suitable review process. The ndings do not justify using these scores as university credentials or substitutes for academic assessment. EST-P4 frames a testable relationship between platform aordances and communication practices, but the eld study did not measure veried learning gains or student production quality over time. Educational use therefore requires a separate outcome design and safeguards against popularity-based ranking.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 226 7.4 Limitations and Robustness Sampling and design. The convenience sample of 52 is drawn from one geographical and listening context. The six institutional categories do not make it representative of Egyptian university students. The design is cross-sectional, and the respondents were not assigned to architectural conditions. Generalisation and causal attribution are therefore limited. Exclusions. The historical analysis retains 52 records after eight exclusions. Identical answers alone cannot establish duplicate respondents; the all-60 sensitivity analysis preserves the positive associations but changes their magnitude (Section 6.4). The original exclusion criterion remains incompletely specied. Interaction-group sizes range from one to 33, making the lowest group's mean especially sensitive to a single response. No latent-group comparison is justied by these descriptive means alone. Measurement. High alpha coexists with poor factor t. A larger sample can improve precision but does not automatically correct misspecied constructs. Self-reported duration and interaction are not automatically behavioural logs. The supplied outputs do not contain timestamps establishing compliance with the platform's intended momentary-assessment schedule. Model dependence. The calibrated contrast is a simulation, not a eld trial. Its sensitivity sweep explores a nite parameter region rather than every plausible model. The reported G0 calibration loss also exceeds the stated target slightly, whereas G1 meets it. Agreement with calibration moments cannot establish

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 227 the validity of all counterfactual predictions. Reproducibility. The supplied R summaries support the eld tables and gures. Cross-le and arithmetic checks establish their consistency, while the new respondent-level script independently reproduces descriptive statistics, alpha, and associations. It does not rerun every statistical model. Recomputing the simulation and Bayesian estimates requires their separate inputs and code. The distinction between source-output checking and full statistical reproduction is maintained in Appendix L. 7.5 Recommendations for Further Research The next empirical stage should rst rene the measurement model and its item content. It should distinguish audience perceptions, observed engagement, independent content-quality judgments, and learning outcomes, rather than combine them under one label. The required sample size should follow the specic analysis and outcome, with explicit allowances for clustering, attrition, and repeated measures where relevant. A subsequent eld comparison should specify the architectural features being changed, assignment procedure, exposure period, primary outcomes, exclusion rules, and analysis before outcome inspection. Repeated observations are needed for H5's dynamics and H6's scheduling question. H7 requires a direct agent task-performance or production endpoint rather than a PB or star-rating proxy. Its paired-network comparison is specied in Section 5.10.1; it is not a completed intervention result. Human learning remains a separate research question.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 228 7.6 Integrated Contribution to Social Media Radio Research The thesis's distinctive contribution is the connection among a radio-like programme, the social circulation surrounding it, and the audience metrics used to evaluate it. The same episode can be encountered through a host, a friend's post, a ranked recommendation, or a shared device. These routes may alter the context of judgment without altering the original audio. EST makes those relationships explicit as architectural and communicative questions. This perspective also establishes what the current evidence can contribute. The questionnaire documents covariation in audience evaluations within one setting. The simulation expresses a proposed architectural comparison. The new propagation schematics connect these levels conceptually, but no event logs or network eects have been added to the empirical results. Keeping these contributions distinct is more informative than treating all three as independent conrmations of the same mechanism. The critical review supports a conditional, not deterministic, interpretation. Radio-public and podcast-platform studies motivate examining distribution and participation (Spinelli & Dann, 2019; Sullivan, 2019). Egyptian audience research establishes local relevance without making this convenience sample representative (Wajih & Al-Yamani, 2024). Experimental algorithm research shows that eects can depend on the direction of a change, prior exposure, and the outcome studied (Gauthier et al., 2026). EST should explain such variation rather than use architecture as a label for every possible result.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 229 7.6.1 Practical Recommendations Matched to the Evidence For producers, preserving source links and the context of excerpts is a reasonable accountability practice, but this study does not quantify its benet. For designers, labels should distinguish audience approval, moderation status, and independently reviewed accuracy. For educators, student-production activities require direct assessment of sourcing and reasoning rather than inference from popularity. These are design implications and evaluation priorities, not established treatment eects. Table 7.2: Findings, Defensible Implications, and Unwarranted Extensions Evidence Defensible implication Unwarranted extension Positive PB associations Study the evaluations jointly and examine overlap Claim that architecture caused the correlations High alpha with poor factor t Retain descriptive reporting and revise measurement Credential students or certify broadcaster accuracy Modelled quality engagement contrast Compare objectives and test the predicted trade-o Claim a universal cost of accurate information Context-specic convenience survey Design replication around reception conditions Generalise to all Egyptian students Proposed correction diagrams Specify events, versions, and outcome denominators Treat schematic paths as observed diusion 7.6.2 A Sequenced Research Programme The rst priority is a complete scoring and measurement record, including language versions and item behaviour. The next stage is the specied computational feature comparison with independently keyed appraisal tasks, assessed production, and recorded network events. Its conclusions concern the model and tested conguration. A separate human study is necessary only for claims about human intervention eects or learning; human predictive delity also requires held-out human outcomes.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 230 This sequence prevents synthetic performance from being interpreted as an already established change in students' competence. An informative follow-up should publish predictions that could fail, record implementation, and compare plausible alternatives. A rating increase without accuracy improvement would rene the mechanism toward cue-based evaluation. No meaningful eect under adequate exposure and precision would challenge the feature-specic prediction. A diversity improvement without engagement loss would challenge a universal trade-o claim. These outcomes would advance EST rather than be treated as reasons to withhold results. 7.6.3 Hallucination as a Measured Phenomenon, Not Only a Bug The planned agent extension could be asked in review whether its outputs are not simply the model hallucinating the desired results. That question is anticipated rather than evaded. In the standard NLP reading, hallucination is a technical failure to be eliminated. In EST, however, hallucination is not a monolith: the three measurement types dened in the methodology (Section 5.10, Section 5.10.12) each point to a distinct process that the design can either guard against as an infrastructure error or report as a substantive quantity. Epistemic/factual fabrication is a task failure against the frozen claim key. Platform-state divergence is an adaptercontract violation that the validator rejects before it can survive. Persona drift is a delity quantity that qualitatively anchored design is intended to keep small. Importantly, a simulation that fabricates a source in defense of a broadcaster it approves of is simultaneously a model artifact and a computational analogue of human motivated reasoning and confabulation phenomena documented across the

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 231 misinformation literature (Pennycook & Rand, 2021). Within EST-P1, such an output is less an embarrassment to be deleted than a measured signature of how trust can be recruited by reputation signals. It oers a prospective way to relate the completed rating measures (which record whether audiences report credibility) to the planned computational extension (which can record whether agents behave as if reputation entitles claims to belief). The theoretical gain depends on measurement: the EFI, PSD, and PDS estimators, with a detector self-check, turn an anecdote of misbehavior into a reported distribution with provenance. The appropriate epistemic status must be preserved. These are planned interpretive tools for a protocol that has not run; they do not retrot meaning onto fabricated numbers, and illustrative or hypothetical values are not reported as executed results. Once genuine logs exist, a higher fabrication rate when appraising claims from apparent high-reputation sources would be interpretable as conrmation bias in the model, not as proof that human students hold that bias. The corresponding defensive claim is therefore disciplined: strict adapter validation and the measured indicators can show that outputs are not free-oating invention, while the estimates themselves remain synthetic and model-conditional. Examining agents in this way also sharpens EST-P4: moderation and integrity tools should distinguish a detector's probabilistic outputs from veried misconduct the same caution that applies to the platform's BRS display in the completed study.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 232 7.7 Mixed-Methods Interpretation: RQ5 and RQ6 The qualitative records extend the study beyond whether ratings covary. RQ5 identies six themes that distinguish reasons for credibility, the attraction of peer voices, the circumstances of listening, participation conditions, student-lived relevance, and delivery quality. These are interpretations of short, researcher-recorded cases, not a representative map of every student experience. Code counts identify corpus coverage rather than strength of causal inuence. For RQ6, the joint display complements the positive interactionPB correlation without contradicting its arithmetic. Some low-interaction cases appreciate calm, familiarity, or concise content; active feedback can include requests for improvement rather than uncomplicated satisfaction. Consequently, treating engagement as the sole quality target would miss some narrated value. At the same time, praise of audio continuity or a familiar voice is not an independent check of informational accuracy. A mixed-methods inference must preserve that distinction rather than use quotations to certify EST. The separate human-gold validation sharpens that boundary. Three independent coders applied the 25-code FGD/self-report codebook with pairwise Cohen's κ of .762 to .861. The local Qwen 7B pass reached micro-F1 .193 zero-shot and .320 with human-gold examples; the Claude rst pass reached .452. None met the prespecied code-level gate for any mechanism code C01 to C05, so E1 to E3 were not eligible; E1 and E2 were computed as exploratory sensitivity checks and E3 was not run. The qualitative material therefore remains an assumption audit and a source

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 233 of candidate design vocabulary, not a calibration target or a test of EST. A randomized-assignment triangulation (Section 6.12.17) checks the same contrast for design dependence. The diversity component, the B×C interaction, and the engagement cost survive all four designs; the BRS component does not. The interpretation follows: the epistemic-rst trade-o is design-robust inside the model, but any statement about BRS diusion must be labelled assignment-dependent. These ndings motivate agent-design dimensions, not deterministic student types. A prole may include conditional willingness to participate, reasons for trusting a source, time constraints, and preferred content, with uncertainty where the record is silent. Student-supplied future accounts should rene these anchors. The planned experiment must then test, rather than assume, that simulated actions resemble held-out human behavior. Its computational task outcomes are distinguished from the completed qualitative analysis and the earlier non-LLM simulation; neither is retrospectively relabelled as a Student Rating treatment eect. 7.7.1 What the Prototype FGD Adds The separate FGD synthesis (Section 6.7) suggests that private practice, listening, collaboration, and publication can represent dierent goals. Co-hosting, institutional visibility, and interface cues may help or constrain participation. These are interpretations of overlapping narratives, not additional rider cases or authenticated transcript ndings. They sharpen questions for EST-P1 and EST-P4 without validating EST-P3 or testing EST-P2. The supplemental generated analysis adds quality cautions and follow-up questions, not recovered primary evidence. In particular, translation errors and unveried attribution do not justify reclassifying its extracts

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 234 as participant testimony or treating narrative repetition as independent support. This contribution supports competing mechanisms in a future rule-based ABM and language-model extension. It cannot supply numerical preference distributions, factual answer keys, or proof of simulator delity. The shared design record in Section 5.9 preserves these boundaries so later results can strengthen, contradict, or leave unresolved the proposed explanations. 7.8 Student Rating and the Meaning of Impact The central student-focused implication is not that favourable stars prove learning. The qualitative accounts describe appraisal, participation, and production interests; the questionnaire records evaluations. Student Rating requires a separate competence measure. NMLS supplies a published measurement basis for human study. In the computational extension, however, independent task accuracy is primary and generated NMLS responses are secondary diagnostics (Section 5.10.12). No human competence gain follows from a dierence between synthetic congurations. The existing ndings can motivate and constrain an explanation of impact, but they do not estimate a Student Rating gain. A model could reproduce PB accurately while failing to reproduce competence or transfer. EST is therefore assessed proposition by proposition: a credible computational mechanism is not automatically a valid learner measure, and neither establishes a general benet for human participants. Agreement with a preferred prediction is not a condition for retaining a result.

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 235 7.9 The Final Calibrated Upgrade: What It Adds and What It Does Not The nal calibrated experiment changes the evidential centre of gravity of the thesis. The measured 52-student wave remains the empirical anchor: it supplies the psychometric relationships, the calibration target, and the substantive reason to care about epistemic architecture. The upgrade adds a reproducible counterfactual model that is explicit about its assumptions and its uncertainty. The strongest nding is not that the epistemic-rst conguration is universally better. It is that the conguration produced a large gain in both evaluative and competence-format Student Ratings while imposing a measurable engagement cost. The trade-o is the nding that gives EST a concrete empirical target. Three qualications follow. First, the model contrast is not a eld treatment eect. The 500 personas are generated from a debiased prior anchored in 52 records; they are not 500 students. The narrow intervals are a property of the simulation, not evidence of population precision. Second, the synthetic NMLS prole is a measurement diagnostic, not a validated measure of human media literacy. The human NMLS remains a prospective instrument, and the competence gain should be read as a model prediction to be tested. Third, the Hamiltonian diagnostic did not move in the direction of lower energy in this implementation. The thermodynamic language therefore remains a formal analogy; the thesis should not present it as a conrmed law. Reporting this result openly is stronger than suppressing it. The upgrade also sharpens the design argument. The BRS and ERIC com-

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 236 ponents account for most of the positive factorial gain, while MORE contributes a smaller but non-trivial share. The mechanisms are partly substitutable, not purely additive. The misinformation stress tests show that the governance bundle is internally coherent under attack. The global sensitivity analysis shows that the model contrast survives a wide parameter sweep and three network topologies, but that it is sensitive to a dogmatically skeptical Bayesian prior. That prior sensitivity is a limitation of the model, not a reason to choose the prior that produces the most favourable answer. For platform design, the practical implication is conditional. If a publisher's objective is raw engagement, the epistemic-rst conguration is not the right benchmark. If the objective is epistemic quality, the conguration is a credible candidate, but its engagement cost must be acknowledged and its human eects must be tested. The thesis therefore argues for explicit objective functions, not for a universal ranking of platforms. The next study should be a longitudinal, pre-registered deployment with independent task-performance measures, not another retrospective reinterpretation of the same 52 records. 7.10 Conclusion The thesis contributes Epistemic Systems Theory, the LOKLOK platform design, and an exploratory account of social media radio evaluations among university students. The eld study reports a PB mean of 5.119, positive associations with ratings and listening context, high internal-consistency coecients, and limitations in factormodel t. The separate simulation reports perceived-quality gains and reduced en-

CHAPTER 7. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 237 gagement under an epistemic-rst conguration, conditional on its assumptions. Six qualitative themes extend these summaries with accounts of credibility, belonging, contextual value, participation, relevance, and delivery. A separate three-coder validation supports the 25-code FGD/self-report codebook, but no mechanism code passed the machine-coding gate, so the qualitative layer remains an assumption audit. The separate FGD synthesis adds four provisional domains and competing participation designs, not an enlarged eld sample or demonstrated behavioural effects. Critical review of the supplemental analysis retains this boundary rather than adopting unsupported claims of transcript recovery or validated mechanisms. The FGD-informed rule-based comparator and LLM extension remain future tests, not completed samples. The defensible conclusion is that architecture, audience judgment, and measurement should be studied together, while the strongest EST propositions remain open to direct empirical testing. The contribution is not weakened by reporting the measurement problems: doing so implements the accountability that the theory requires and denes what a stronger subsequent test must establish. Chapter summary. The discussion argues that EST is a useful design framework but remains unproven. The simulation supports a conditional epistemic engagement trade-o and identies which mechanisms are active; it does not support claims about real students or population representativeness. The thesis contributes a transparent bridge from theory to a testable design, and it species the eld study needed to test EST properly.
